newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts' comments on Akzo Nobel results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' comments on Akzo Nobel results.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV on Friday reported a 2.4 percent rise in first quarter 1997 net profit to 340 million guilders. Analysts had forecast a range of between 332 million and 380 million guilders.
Below is a collection of analysts' comments on the results.

"Overall, these figures are encouraging. I think it's a good start to a better year. To me, chemicals are the main eye-catcher, far better than expected, outstanding. Probably, the effects of the costly restructurings are trickling through, very good if sustainable.

Pharma is somewhat disappointing, but I guess that can be blamed on introduction costs of (the new antidepression drug) Remeron, meaning it's only temporary. The pill scare should not have had much additional impact as it also affected the first quarter of last year. I 'll wait till the conference call before possibly changing my estimates," said Schouten.
TONY COX, KLEINWORT BENSON IN LONDON:

"First reaction is that they are a little disappointing and primarily in the two so-called high quality units, coatings and pharmaceuticals. Coatings was considerably worse than expected and a big disappointment particularly as it's the first quarter. Given the huge increase in pharmaceuticals in the fourth quarter last year, this time the rise was much smaller. Overall, with the huge benefit from favourable currency moves they've had, it's a disappointing performance."

"The share price shows it's a disappointment. Especially in pharma, where I had expected income from Organon's new products to compensate for the introduction costs. Fibres' deterioration was worse, coatings improved less than I had expected. Chemicals performed better, but benefited from the dollar. The conference call should say if the turnaround of the new drugs will come soon, I won't modify estimates till then."
